messages:
Acme-CS: Hey team — our customer Acme started seeing 401 invalid_api_key errors from our API this morning after they rotated keys in their vault. They can reproduce with curl. Filing because it's blocking their rollout.

Acme-CS: sample curl they ran (redacted key):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123...XYZ\" \"https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate\"
```

jess: thanks — can you paste the full verbose response (with headers) and the x-request-id from the response headers? also confirm if they used the console to rotate or an API call.

Acme-CS: here's the verbose response (response headers redacted except ids) — they rotated via console.
```
* Connected to api.redwood.inference (13.32.187.9) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.inference
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123...XYZ
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-length: 0
< x-request-id: rq_acme_7f9d3
< x-error-code: invalid_api_key
<
```

ben: two quick questions: 1) is the customer using our SDK or a direct curl? 2) can they echo the key bytes to make sure there are no stray control chars? e.g. `echo -n \"$KEY\" | xxd -g 1` or `printf \"%q\" \"$KEY\"` — sometimes copy/paste adds CR/LF.

Acme-CS: they're on curl right now from their CI. They ran `echo -n \"$ACME_KEY\" | xxd -g 1 -l 40` and posted the output: there was a trailing `0d` byte at the end (CR). They said their secrets manager copy button is on Windows.

ryan: that explains it — our token validation is strict (no extra bytes). A trailing \r (0x0d) will change the HMAC/content and become invalid. Also note some folks paste into an Authorization header with an extra newline which ends up being part of the header value in some HTTP client libs. Two remediation paths: rotate the key (recommended) and ensure the secret stored in vault/CI pipeline is trimmed, or keep same key and strip control chars in their deploy.

jess: quick repro I did locally:
```
# with CR at end (bad)
KEY_BAD=$'sk_live_TESTABC123\r'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H \"x-api-key: $KEY_BAD\" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/health
# -> 401

# trimmed (good)
KEY_GOOD=$(echo -n \"$KEY_BAD\" | tr -d '\r')
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H \"x-api-key: $KEY_GOOD\" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/health
# -> 200
```

jess: notes and guidance for Acme: use the `x-api-key` header (preferred) or `Authorization: Bearer <token>` but make sure the value has no surrounding quotes or control chars. Verify length with `echo -n $KEY | wc -c` (should match the expected length we provided when issuing the key). If they rotate in the console, the old key is immediately revoked — so ensure the pipeline picks up the new secret.

Acme-CS: we rotated the key and updated their k8s secret (we trimmed CRLF before applying). After deploy their requests succeeded. They reported the following confirm log: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and generation returns as expected.

ben: root cause summary: customer copied API key from UI on Windows which added a trailing CR (\r). The CI secret had the control char, causing strict validation to fail with invalid_api_key.

ryan: suggestions to reduce recurrence: 1) on our docs page add a short note about trimming/avoiding copy artifacts, 2) on the console after copying show a small toast like \"Key copied — trimmed for CR/LF\" or offering a download button, 3) add a helpful error hint in the 401 body when we detect non-printable trailing bytes (non-sensitive logging only).

Acme-CS: thanks all — they are unblocked. :tada:

support-bot: This thread will be closed in 24h unless there are further updates.
